entry.title: Ravda Beach, Nessebar
entry.summary: Ravda is a quieter resort village south of Nessebar with a long sandy beach and shallow water. It is more relaxed than Sunny Beach, with a mix of hotels, restaurants and local life.

entry.title: Debeli Rtic Beach
entry.summary: Debeli rtic is a protected headland at the north-western tip of the Slovenian coast, near the Italian border, with low cliffs, woodland and small pebble coves. It is a natural monument and much quieter than the resorts to the south.

entry.title: Simonov Zaliv Beach, Izola
entry.summary: Simonov zaliv is a bay just west of Izola with a grassy lawn, a pebble and concrete shore and clear water, close to the remains of the Roman port of Haliaetum. It is one of the more relaxed organised beaches on the coast.

entry.title: Moon Bay (Mesecev Zaliv), Strunjan
entry.summary: Moon Bay is a crescent-shaped pebble cove below the Strunjan cliff, the highest on the Slovenian coast, inside Strunjan Landscape Park. A steep path leads down from the cliff top, and there are no buildings on the bay.

entry.title: Fiesa Beach
entry.summary: Fiesa is a small pebble bay below green slopes between Piran and Strunjan, next to two small lakes that are a protected natural area. It is quieter than Piran and Portoroz, and you can walk there along the coast path from Piran.

entry.title: Portoroz Central Beach
entry.summary: Portoroz has the largest organised beach in Slovenia, a sand-covered stretch in front of the resort hotels with shallow, calm water. It is lively and well equipped, and suits families with small children.

entry.title: Punta Beach, Piran
entry.summary: Swimming in Piran means stepping off the stone and concrete platforms that run around the tip of the old town, below the lighthouse and the church of St Clement. The water is clear and deep close to shore, with the medieval town right behind you.

entry.title: Neptun Beach
entry.summary: Neptun is a green, low-rise resort north of Mangalia, set around small lakes and woodland, with a sandy beach that is usually calmer than Mamaia. Olimp and the Jupiter, Venus and Saturn resorts continue along the same stretch of coast.

entry.title: Eforie Nord Beach
entry.summary: Eforie Nord is a long-established spa resort just south of Constanta, between the sea and Lake Techirghiol, whose mineral mud is used in local treatments. The beach is wide and sandy, with calm, shallow water that suits families.

entry.title: Sulina Beach
entry.summary: Sulina is the easternmost town in Romania, where the Danube meets the Black Sea, and there is no road to it: you arrive by boat from Tulcea. Its beach is a long, wide stretch of fine sand a short way from town and is rarely crowded.

entry.title: Gura Portitei Beach
entry.summary: Gura Portitei is a narrow sand spit between the Black Sea and Lake Golovita, inside the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve. Most visitors arrive by boat from Jurilovca, and the beach feels remote, with a small holiday village and wide, empty sand.

entry.title: Corbu Beach
entry.summary: Corbu is one of the last wild beaches on the Romanian coast, a long strip of fine sand north of Navodari with no hotels on the shore. It is reached by an unpaved road, and the space and quiet draw campers and people escaping the big resorts.

entry.title: Costinesti Beach
entry.summary: Costinesti is a lively resort popular with students and young travellers, with a sandy beach backed by low cliffs. North of the resort, the rusting wreck of the cargo ship Evangelia sits just offshore and is one of the best-known sights on the coast.

entry.title: 2 Mai Beach
entry.summary: 2 Mai is a small fishing village between Mangalia and Vama Veche, with a calmer, more family-friendly beach than its lively neighbour. Guesthouses take the place of big hotels, and part of the shore has long been used as a naturist area.

entry.title: Vama Veche Beach
entry.summary: Vama Veche is the last village before the Bulgarian border and has long had a reputation as the free-spirited, bohemian beach of Romania. The sand is mixed with shells, bars play live music into the night, and some visitors still camp near the shore.

entry.title: Mamaia Beach, Constanta
entry.summary: Mamaia is the best-known resort in Romania, a strip of fine sand about 8 km long between the Black Sea and Lake Siutghiol, just north of Constanta. The water is shallow and calm on most days, and the shore is lined with hotels, sunbed concessions and bars.

entry.title: Ladies Beach, Kusadasi
entry.summary: Ladies Beach is a popular beach south of Kusadasi town, with a long stretch of sand and small pebbles, beach clubs and shallow water. It is lively in summer, easy to reach by dolmus from the centre, and good for sunsets over the sea.

entry.title: Olympos Beach, Kemer
entry.summary: Olympos beach is a long stretch of pebbles and coarse sand at the mouth of a pine-covered valley, with mountains rising behind and the ruins of the ancient city of Olympos beside it. It feels quiet and wild, with tree-house lodges and small cafes nearby.

entry.title: Golden Sands Beach, Varna
entry.summary: Golden Sands is one of the largest Bulgarian resorts, set inside a nature park north of Varna. The beach is a wide band of fine sand with shallow water, and there are many bars, rides and water sports.

entry.title: Primorsko Beach, Primorsko
entry.summary: Primorsko is a resort town on the southern Black Sea coast with long sandy beaches, shallow water and a seafront promenade. It is popular with families and young people and has forested hills behind.

entry.title: Pomorie Beach, Pomorie
entry.summary: Pomorie sits on a narrow peninsula, and its sandy beaches are lined with groynes and backed by apartments and promenades. The town is known for its salt lake and mineral spa, and it is quieter than Sunny Beach.

entry.title: Saints Constantine and Helena Beach, Varna
entry.summary: Saints Constantine and Helena is the oldest seaside resort in Bulgaria, set in a park north of Varna. The beaches are small and sandy and sit below hotels and gardens, with a relaxed spa-resort feel.

entry.title: Varna City Beach, Varna
entry.summary: Varna city beach is a long strip of sand below the Sea Garden, within walking distance of the centre. It is easy to reach and lively in summer, and the water can be wavy when the wind blows from the east.

entry.title: Byala Beach, Byala
entry.summary: Byala is a small town on the northern Black Sea coast with a sandy beach, a wooden pier and calm water. It is low-key, with a harbour feel and fewer large hotels than the main resorts.

entry.title: Chernomorets Beach, Sozopol
entry.summary: Chernomorets is a village beach north of Sozopol with a long curve of sand and rows of sunbeds below a low headland. It is quieter than the big resorts and suits families who want shallow water.

entry.title: Vlas Beach, Sveti Vlas
entry.summary: Sveti Vlas is a resort town at the northern end of Sunny Beach bay, with a sandy beach edged by rocks and dune grass. It is calmer than Sunny Beach and sits below the green slopes of the Balkan foothills.

entry.title: Silistar Beach, Tsarevo
entry.summary: Silistar is a quiet sandy beach on the far southern coast, close to the Strandzha Nature Park and the Turkish border region. It has a simple, uncrowded feel, with forested hills behind and few buildings nearby.

entry.title: Kavatsite Beach, Sozopol
entry.summary: Kavatsite is a long sandy beach north of Sozopol, backed by dunes and a pine camping area. The water is shallow and calm, and the atmosphere is relaxed and informal.

entry.title: Krapets Beach, Shabla
entry.summary: Krapets is a small village on the northern coast near Shabla with a long sandy beach and few visitors. It is simple and low-key, with calm water in summer and a very different feel from the big resorts.

entry.title: Arkutino Beach, Primorsko
entry.summary: Arkutino is a sandy beach between Sozopol and Primorsko, set next to Arkutino lake and the Ropotamo nature reserve. It is calmer than the resort strips, with dunes and pines behind the sand.
